summary: Repo already has this exact item with proof and verification (BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md items 188/229/266: isosceles law, D=U at p≡1(4), U−D=2 at p≡3(4)); not promoted to DISCOVERIES. Re-proved: 4/n=2/x+1/z ⟺ (4x−2n)(4z−n)=2n², A=2d, B=n²/d (d | n²), integrality forces only B≡−n (mod 4); for odd n this holds iff n has a prime factor ≡3 (mod 4) (n≡3: take B=1), even n always — so failure ⟺ all prime factors ≡1 (mod 4) (PROVED). CERTIFIED for 2≤n≤3000 by the divisor test (344 failures = A004613 minus 1) and an independent brute force for n≤400, 0 mismatches. One level beyond: it is a fixed-modulus (mod 4) genus obstruction on a rational curve of the surface — an exact B1/T1-type toy (all divisors of n² ≡1 mod 4), and the same failure set as the two-term problem 4/n=1/a+1/b; it says nothing about the growing-modulus certificate lines.
next: Optional: one-paragraph lemma in a paper appendix; no ES lead.

summary: Recomputed the word sieve (scripts/z52b_fingerprint_words.c, n≤3·10⁶, 11 s; ESC(5)=6 reproduced) and U(p) from data/z52b/raw (p≤2·10⁵); dyadic windows of primes p≡1 (4). ESC/log²p: mean drifts slowly down 0.668→0.607 (10³→3·10⁶), window minimum stabilises at 0.096–0.13 from 6·10⁴ on (min/mean 0.15–0.21), sd(log ESC) falls 0.41→0.26; the global minima are the known hard primes (2521: 0.065; 9601, 83449). U/log²p has mean rising 0.81→1.17 (U ≍ log³p, ET), min/mean 0.17–0.31; ESC ≈ 0.57·U on average (corr of logs 0.85), ESC/U ∈ [0.25, 3]. So ESC is the log²-scaled count with a stable floor ≈0.1·log²p in range — a clean calibration constant, but no structure beyond the known hard primes.
next: None needed; if used as a heuristic target, quote min ESC/log²p ≈ 0.10 (p ∈ [6·10⁴, 3·10⁶]).

summary: GEOMETRY_ES.md §2.1–2.2 already gives the minimal resolution Bl₆ℙ² (Cayley model, 3 coordinate points + 3 collinear V_k), the four nodes (root system 4A1, all four (−2)-curves = lines X_i=0, σ=0), the nine rational lines and §3.1 the conic bundles F1–F3 (split). Did the lattice step (scripts/z52d_audit2_B1_conics.py): exactly 9 nef classes with F²=0, −K·F=2 on the resolution — H−V_k (=F1, fix u_k), H−p_k (=F2, u_i/u_j=λ), 2H−(4 pts) (=F3, planes through M_k) — i.e. 3 orbits under the S₃ fixing P, 2 orbits (6+3: planes through an edge / through an M-line) under the full S₄; all defined over ℚ (everything is split), each with explicit reducible fibres (l+l′, l+N+l′, N+N′+2E). So F1–F3 are provably all conic-bundle structures (a small completion of GEOMETRY §3.1); ET Type I/II are F1 fibres (fix the denominator), the (★) words are F2 fibres (λ=B/u). Nothing new for ES.
next: Optional one-line addendum to GEOMETRY_ES §3.1: the 9 classes exhaust conic bundles.

summary: Not done in the repo (sibling items only in BRAINSTORM/z52b_signature.md #7, z52b_translate.md #299, untested). Did the step (scripts/z52d_audit2_B1_symcoords.py): a root x of T³−s1T²+s2T−ps2/4 forces s2 = 4x²(s1−x)/(4x−p), and the remaining quadratic must have square discriminant — i.e. the (s1,s2) search is literally 'fix x, solve the two-term problem'; the box search reproduces the full solution sets at p = 5, 13, 17. Over all primes p≡1 (4) < 3000, min s1 ≥ 1.014·p^{3/2} (consistent with HARDNESS_MAP's max(x,y,z) > p^{3/2}/2), so there are no 'small' (s1,s2) and the cubic search is costlier than the divisor search; the only forced constraints are 4 | s2 and the trivial mod-p factorisation T(T²−s1T+s2). Pure reparametrisation.

HARDNESS_MAP.md §A7 (residue DP over 4t states after factoring; Lenstra / Coppersmith–Howgrave-Graham–Nagaraj divisors-in-residue-classes, citing BRAINSTORM/z31_complexity.md) already gives the algorithmic picture; the subset-product form is in B1_LINE.md:235 and BRAINSTORM/z31_zero_sum.md. The requested bounds, derived: per slice with N = ∏q_i^{a_i} (k = ω(N)), the quotient set {ab⁻¹ : ab | N} = {∏q_i^{c_i} : |c_i| ≤ a_i}, so deciding −1 ∈ Q costs O(|G|·Σ(2a_i+1)) by DP over G = (ℤ/e)^×, or O(∏(2a_i+1)^{1/2}·k) ≈ 3^{k/2} by meet-in-the-middle (FPT in k); for G of exponent 2 it is linear algebra over 𝔽₂ (poly). Since ω(N) ≈ log log p, the per-slice search is never the bottleneck — existence (and factoring) is, so the parameterisation says nothing about ES.

BRAINSTORM/padic_adelic_scaling.md (route (i) 'adelic volume main term', Prop A scaling lemma) and BRAINSTORM/markoff_hasse_failures_vs_es.md F3/F4 already did this: local densities are n-flat for ℓ ≠ p (u ↦ u/n isomorphism of integral models), while true counts vary ×14 across classes mod 840 with the six Mordell square classes lowest — so no adelic/BM window volume sees the main fluctuation; the p-dependent main terms in use are M₀ = (3/(2π²))log²p / M_BM (BM_CORRECTED_COUNT §2) and the RESIDUE_HARDNESS class factor. Re-checked numerically (scripts/z52d_audit2_B1_localdens.py): #U_n(ℤ/m)/m² identical for n ∈ {13,17,29,37,41} at m = 3,9,5,25,7,49,8,16, and the ratios grow with k (1.11→1.33 at ℓ = 3; 1.25→1.375 at 2) because the surface is nodal — naive local densities do not converge, the volume needs a height-truncated (log-K3) regularisation, which is where the log² comes from. Nothing new.

Repo: DEDEKIND_ES.md §3/§6 (C1: Dedekind sums mod a fixed modulus = Jacobi symbol only; C2: s(A,p) fixes r−r′, the needed symmetric invariant r+r′ 'obeys no reciprocity law'; C4: Knopp/Hecke generalised sums give σ(N)-type data) and z52_deep_thin_pointwise_opus.md (χ-blind charge); twisted sums were not tested. Did it (scripts/z52d_audit2_B1_twdedekind.py, all A at p = 409, 1009, 2521): Berndt-type s(a,c;χ) = Σχ(n)B̄1(n/k)B̄1(an/ck) vanish identically for odd χ (|·| < 10⁻¹³) and are odd in a ↦ −a for even χ, so like s they cannot see the even invariant r+r′; the even-in-a sums Σχ(n)B̄1(n/k)B̄2(an/ck) (odd χ = χ₋₄, χ₋₈) have R² ≤ 0.004 for r+r′ or log(r+r′), and no twisted sum separates ES₅ certificates from other QNR A (AUC 0.08–0.69, erratic; only 4–10 certificates per p), whereas plain s gives AUC 0.98 — the known (D3) r−r′ effect. Structural reason: the parity of the Bernoulli-function product fixes the a ↦ −a parity, and the even ones carry no CF-length information here.
next: None (a χ-sensitive reciprocity law would still give only the quadratic layer, CLASS_FORCING Thm 2.1).

summary: Partly in repo (χ_p count law, BRAINSTORM/z52b_fingerprint.md #4; R-zeros have small h(−4p), #131; BM_LVALUE.md: M_BM depends on L(1,χ_p) and p mod 8); for p≡1 (4) N(ε_p) = −1 and the 2-rank of Cl(−4p) is 1 always, so those κ are constant. Did the correlation on all 103 500 primes p≡1 (4) ≤ 3·10⁶ (ESC and (★) counts from the word sieve; scripts/z52d_audit2_B1_kappa.py) with κ ∈ {L(1,χ_p), L(1,χ₋₄ₚ) ∝ h(−4p)/√p, least QNR, 4|h(−4p) (p≡1 (8)), 8|h(−4p) (Barrucand–Cohn), p mod 3}: over all p the invariants look strong (top quintile of h(−4p): min ESC/log²p 0.283 vs 0.096, no (★)-zeros; joint R² 0.37), but restricted to the 6 355 Mordell-hard primes > 10⁵ the effects collapse (corr with L(1,χ₋₄ₚ) +0.12; min ESC/log²p 0.096–0.135 in every quintile of every κ; the 4 (★)-zeros spread across quintiles). So the apparent 'regular' sets are the mod-840 identity classes in disguise; no candidate κ carves out Mordell-hard primes with a better worst case. Range: p ≤ 3·10⁶, not 10⁸.
next: None; any future κ test must condition on the Mordell-hard classes.

summary: Read arXiv:2003.13229 (Dagal, math.HO, 8 pp.): Thm 5.1 rewriter 1/s + 1/(rs) = 1/(qr) + 1/(qs), r = q+d, s = qr−d — an elementary special case of the 'pivot' (hold one denominator, re-split the other two) already studied in Q3_PIVOT.md. Applied to all 8 334 solutions of 4/p for primes p≡1 (4) < 3000 (scripts/z52d_audit2_B1_dagal.py, 25 002 denominator pairs): no pair admits a Dagal move at all (0 edges); among all n < 1200 such moves occur for many composites but at only two primes (11, 19), and exactness/positivity/three terms are trivially preserved when they do. The general pivot graph on U_p is disconnected at 207 of 211 primes p≡1 (4) < 3000 (mean 8.4 components), consistent with Q3_PIVOT's traps; nothing reaches new congruence classes.

Took the concrete reading: e-slice event (−1 ∈ {ab⁻¹ mod e : ab | N}, N = (p+e)/4) as a function of the residue multiset of N's prime factors; for 400 random primes p≡1 (4) in [10⁶, 2·10⁶] and all prime e < 60, replaced one prime factor's class by each other class (scripts/z52d_audit2_B1_intervene.py): a hit flips in 18.8% of single-factor interventions, a miss in 28.8%, and 62% of the 2 136 hit slices are killed by some single substitution. Caveat that makes the item weak: the intervention cannot hold the algebraic model fixed — changing one factor of N changes p (generally to a non-prime), so this is synthetic sensitivity, not a causal statement about primes. It quantifies the known picture (events depend on factor classes only; single large factors are private, CLASS_FORCING Thm 5.2, SYNTHESIS_SPARKS8 Lemma 2.3) and adds nothing for ES.

EXSET_BEYOND_CRT.md §4.3 (door D7) already answers the step's question: Montgomery–Vaughan's x^{1−δ} needs a singular series bounded below plus an L²-small minor-arc error, whereas the ES count is a sum of shifted restricted divisor functions whose normalised variance is not o(1/polylog) (Linnik-type fluctuations), so no L²-small reformulation exists; the ES side is FRONTIER §1/§5.1 (Vaughan exp(−c log^{2/3}), internal 3/4, sharp for CRT architectures). One level beyond (Assessment): this is B3 in exceptional-set form — with main term ≍ log²n and variance ≥ main term, Chebyshev gives only E ≪ N/log²N, so any power saving needs a non-variance (sieve/large-sieve over moduli) mechanism; and for f(n) (Type I/II) the odd squares force E ≥ √N anyway. Catalog facts (MV 1975, Chudakov–van der Corput–Estermann, 4·10¹⁸) are standard.

Already settled in the repo: every reduced ET/identity family (a,b) needs (ab/p) = −1 (Lemma CT, POINTWISE_SIZE; the (★) pair (u,B) needs χ₋₄ᵤ_B(p) = −1 identically, FRONTIER §2.2), so for any finite set of families all fail at every p ≡ 1 (mod L) with L = 24·∏8ab (all their primes are residues) — HARDNESS_MAP.md l.230 proves this unconditionally, FRONTIER B1/Mordell–Schinzel for polynomial families, B2 Thm 2.2(iii) for finite slice menus. Hence two (or finitely many) families with complementary failure sets cannot exist; their Legendre conditions all vanish on the same 'square-mimicking' class. Not re-computed beyond checking the cited statements; nothing new.

Structure already in BRAINSTORM/corr_parity_layers.md (slice classes hit / prime / Q quadratic-sign / Q′ higher-order / A '−1 ∈ H but no hit'), gon_incidence_kloosterman.md (c5) and the reciprocity window (J)64 (CAP_POINTWISE: (e/p) = −1 forces −1 ∈ ⟨primes of N⟩). Key observation: for p ≡ 1 (4) the Type II e-slice has e ≡ 3 (4), so v₂(e−1) = 1 and '−1 ∈ ⟨factors⟩ ⟺ |H| even' is exactly 'some prime factor of N is a QNR mod e' — the 2-adic-order/Artin angle degenerates to the quadratic layer. Computed (scripts/z52d_audit2_B1_eslice_parity.py; 300 Mordell-hard primes in [10⁶, 3·10⁶], all prime e < 400, 12 000 slices; equivalence asserted, and −1 ∈ H whenever (e/p) = −1, both with 0 exceptions): P(−1 ∈ H) = 0.663, P(hit) = 0.227, P(no hit | −1 ∈ H) = 0.658 — two thirds of the slices passing the necessary condition still miss (type A, the size lottery). Nothing beyond the known parity/class split.

This is exactly the genus split of SINGLE_P_COUNT.md §2 (Lemma 2.1: R = M_gen + X, M_gen = the order-≤2 character part mod q = 4uB, explicit in p mod 8 and Legendre symbols; T1 lives entirely in M_gen) and BM_CORRECTED_COUNT.md §1–2 (the Brauer class is one of the s(q) real characters; M_BM ≥ (3/(16π²) − o(1))log²p unconditionally). The proof-attempt question ('can a genus-style main term dominate pointwise?') is answered there: the needed (U) |X(p)| < M_gen(p) is false at the 14 (★)-failures (X = −M_gen), GRH gives only M_gen ≥ (1 − o(1))log log p ((J)98), and no standard conjecture is known to imply the one-sided H⁻_BM (FRONTIER §2.4). Nothing new to add; not recomputed.

Did the tabulation with repo/own numbers at p ≈ 1.5·10⁵ (windows from scripts/z52d_audit2_B1_esc.py; L = log p ≈ 11.9): (★) mean R ≈ 0.17L² ≈ 24 over (p/4)L ≈ 4.5·10⁵ trial events (PARITY_AUDIT trial form) → log(main)/log(trials) ≈ 0.25; ESC words ≈ 0.62L² ≈ 88 over ≈ p log p ≈ 1.8·10⁶ (t,u) pairs → 0.31; full count U ≈ 1.17L² ≈ 166 over ≈ p/2 choices of x → 0.46; ES₅ ≈ (45/(8π²))L² over p values of A → ≈ 0.34; binary Goldbach at 10⁶: ≈ 7·10³ over 7.8·10⁴ → ≈ 0.79 (estimates, EVIDENCE). Every ES form has sparsity ≈ k·log log p/log p → 0, and the index is encoding-dependent (grouping trials into slices or x-fibres changes the denominator without changing the problem), so the 'least sparse' form (full U over x-fibres) is just the coarsest grouping. The substantive content — polylog main term vs power trials, no known every-n theorem at that scale — is already FRONTIER §3 M1a / (J)94 and the (J)103 survey.
